title: Base change commutes with a fibre product
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $k'/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. There is a canonical isomorphism of $k'$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base] $(X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k' \cong (X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k')\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}(Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k')$, where each fibre product and base change is as in [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-pc-base-change], compatible with the projections to the two base-changed factors.

source.place: Tag 038F and the fibre-product base-change identifications used in Tag 054P

proof.text: Write $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ and $Y_{k'}=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ (base changes [def-pc-base-change], with projections $f_{k'}:X_{k'}\to X$, $\mathrm{pr}:X_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ and $g_{k'}:Y_{k'}\to Y$, $\mathrm{pr}:Y_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$), $p,q$ for the projections of $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y$, and $A=(X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ with projections $r:A\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y$, $s:A\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$. By the universal property of $X_{k'}$ [def-pc-fibre-product] there are unique $\pi_X=(p\circ r,s):A\to X_{k'}$ and $\pi_Y=(q\circ r,s):A\to Y_{k'}$, and $\mathrm{pr}\circ\pi_X=s=\mathrm{pr}\circ\pi_Y$. Claim: $(A,\pi_X,\pi_Y)$ is a fibre product of $X_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'\leftarrow Y_{k'}$. Given a scheme $T$ and $\alpha:T\to X_{k'}$, $\beta:T\to Y_{k'}$ with $\mathrm{pr}\circ\alpha=\mathrm{pr}\circ\beta=:t$, the morphisms $f_{k'}\circ\alpha:T\to X$ and $g_{k'}\circ\beta:T\to Y$ have the same composite $T\xrightarrow{t}\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so give $c=(f_{k'}\alpha,g_{k'}\beta):T\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y$, and $c$ and $t$ agree over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so give $\gamma=(c,t):T\to A$. Then $\pi_X\circ\gamma$ has components $p\circ c=f_{k'}\circ\alpha$ and $s\circ\gamma=t=\mathrm{pr}\circ\alpha$, so $\pi_X\circ\gamma=\alpha$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of $X_{k'}$; likewise $\pi_Y\circ\gamma=\beta$. If $\gamma':T\to A$ also satisfies $\pi_X\gamma'=\alpha$, $\pi_Y\gamma'=\beta$, then $s\gamma'=\mathrm{pr}\,\alpha=t$, $p r\gamma'=f_{k'}\alpha$ and $q r\gamma'=g_{k'}\beta$, so $r\gamma'=c$ and $\gamma'=\gamma$ by the uniqueness clauses for $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y$ and $A$. This proves the claim.

proof.text: Let $B=X_{k'}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}Y_{k'}$ be the chosen fibre product with its projections. By step 1, $(A,\pi_X,\pi_Y)$ is also a fibre product of $X_{k'}$ and $Y_{k'}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k'$, so by the uniqueness clause of [def-pc-fibre-product] there is a unique isomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ compatible with the projections to $X_{k'}$ and $Y_{k'}$. The structure morphism of $A$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is $s=\mathrm{pr}\circ\pi_X$ and that of $B$ is $\mathrm{pr}\circ(\text{first projection})$, so $\varphi$ is a morphism of $k'$-schemes; this is the canonical isomorphism of the statement.

lean.statement: theorem baseChange_product {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Scheme.Spec.obj (op (CommRingCat.of k))) (g : Y ⟶ Scheme.Spec.obj (op (CommRingCat.of k))) : let i : Scheme.Spec.obj (op (CommRingCat.of k')) ⟶ Scheme.Spec.obj (op (CommRingCat.of k)) := Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')).op let P : Scheme.{u} := pullback f g let hP : P ⟶ Scheme.Spec.obj (op (CommRingCat.of k)) := pullback.snd f g ≫ g let A : Scheme.{u} := pullback hP i let B : Scheme.{u} := pullback (pullback.snd f i) (pullback.snd g i) ∃ e : A ≅ B, e.hom ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.snd f i) (pullback.snd g i) ≫ pullback.fst f i = pullback.fst hP i ≫ pullback.fst f g ∧ e.hom ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.snd f i) (pullback.snd g i) ≫ pullback.snd f i = pullback.snd hP i ∧ e.hom ≫ pullback.snd (pullback.snd f i) (pullback.snd g i) ≫ pullback.fst g i = pullback.fst hP i ≫ pullback.snd f g ∧ e.hom ≫ pullback.snd (pullback.snd f i) (pullback.snd g i) ≫ pullback.snd g i = pullback.snd hP i
